question:
During triage in Observability Distributed Tracing SRE, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: Distributed Trace Context Dropped Across Asynchronous Thread Handoff".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: Thread-local storage (or contextvars) does not automatically propagate to new OS threads or celery worker tasks unless explicitly passed. ---

Each service correctly propagated the W3C traceparent header, but two services disagreed on which header name to use, so downstream spans were created under a brand-new trace ID instead of merging with the original.
Spans were sampled at 1% to reduce overhead, so most of the requests in the reported trace simply were never recorded in the first place, not dropped mid-flight.
The tracing SDK batched spans and flushed them every 30 seconds, so a short-lived async task's spans were queued but the process exited before the batch was ever exported.

explanation:
Root Cause: Thread-local storage (or contextvars) does not automatically propagate to new OS threads or celery worker tasks unless explicitly passed. ---

By sampling only a small percentage of requests for tracing, on the assumption that a lower sampling rate alone keeps trace context intact across every async boundary.
By logging a request ID to stdout on every service, trusting that grepping logs later is equivalent to having a propagated distributed trace.
By storing trace context in a global mutable variable shared across all requests, since a single shared value is assumed to be enough state for concurrent traces.
